A baby hippo found desperately nudging its dead mother at a lake in Kenya over the weekend is now being hand-reared at a wildlife sanctuary after being rescued.

Bumpy was discovered on May 2, 2026 at Naivasha’s Oloiden Resort in south-central Kenya. The Kenya Wildlife Service Vet and Capture team were alerted to reports of an orphaned baby hippo in the area and quickly sprang into action, eventually coming upon the corpse of Bumpy’s mother.
The calf, which has been named Bumpy, was "just days old" when it became orphaned, according to Sheldrick Wildlife Trust, a charity whose keepers are now taking care of it.

original_article.description: The baby hippo, which has been named Bumpy, was found clinging to its lifeless mother at a lake.
original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
A baby hippo found desperately nudging its dead mother at a lake in Kenya over the weekend is now being hand-reared at a wildlife sanctuary after being rescued.

The calf, which has been named Bumpy, was "just days old" when it became orphaned, according to Sheldrick Wildlife Trust, a charity whose keepers are now taking care of it.

The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS), which rescued the calf and handed it over to the wildlife charity for specialised care, said the mother may have died from natural causes.

Sheldrick said it was possible that the hippo's mother died in a "territorial fight... protecting her calf, as infanticide is common in hippo society".

KWS said rescuing the calf from the water was a "logistical challenge", with the calf clinging to its dead mother. It said it had to make a "painful decision" to use the decomposing body "as the only anchor to safely reach the calf".

According to Sheldrick, the mother had been dead for more than a day or longer, based on the level of decomposition.

After being rescued, the baby hippo spent its first night at a nursery in the capital Nairobi, being fed on milk and swaddled in a blanket.

The charity says Bumpy "was clearly desperate for comfort and connection" and has been glued to his keepers ever since.

The calf was later flown by helicopter to Sheldrick's Kaluku sanctuary near Tsavo East National Park, to be taken care of until it is ready to be released into the wild.

The sanctuary has been sharing Bumpy's story and photos at its new location – at a pool near the Athi River which runs through the park.

"[Bumpy] spends a lot of the day submerged - but never alone. A rather waterlogged keeper is by his side throughout the day, in the water or on the ground," Sheldrick adds.

"He is a very snuggly creature and is happiest when nestled on or against someone," the sanctuary adds, alongside a photo of the hippo with its head on the keeper's lap.

Bumpy joins another young hippo at Kaluku who is nearly a year old, although they are being kept in different areas, the sanctuary says.

Both are expected to be released when they grow up to join other hippos living in the wild.

In the wild, a hippo calf nurses for uo to a year or more but remains closely attached to its mother for several years until around sexual maturity, according to wildlife experts.

Founded in 1977, the Sheldrick Wildlife is renowned for its care of orphaned elephants and rhinos, rescuing and reintegrating them into the wild.

Go to BBC

---

[Lähde: Dexerto]
Bumpy is a baby hippo who was rescued after his mother died. Now he’s being taken care of at the Sheldrick Wildlife Trust, and his story is warming hearts across the internet.

Bumpy was discovered on May 2, 2026 at Naivasha’s Oloiden Resort in south-central Kenya. The Kenya Wildlife Service Vet and Capture team were alerted to reports of an orphaned baby hippo in the area and quickly sprang into action, eventually coming upon the corpse of Bumpy’s mother.

A description of Bumpy’s rescue on the Trust’s official website claims the infant “clearly didn’t understand the situation,” saying he was “calling out to his mother and nudging her with his blunt little nose, desperately hoping for a response.”

Meet Bumpy! This enchanting little chap was rescued over the weekend. His mother likely died defending him in a territorial fight and when the Kenya Wildlife Service found him, he was huddled beside her body. They rescued him and placed him in our care.This was Bumpy's first… pic.twitter.com/qODt1z5GEI

The Sheldrick Wildlife Trust believes his mother had died from a territorial battle the day prior, saying she was likely attempting to protect her baby during the struggle.

Rescuers bundled up baby Bumpy in a cherry red blanket and brought him to the Nairobi Nursery, where he spent his first night guzzling down milk and snuggling into the side of Keeper Simon.

The next morning, he was transported to Kalaku by helicopter. The Trust described him as the “perfect passenger,” saying he “scrambled right into Keeper Joseph’s lap and spent most of the trip chattering in little hippo grunts.”

Yesterday, we introduced you to our newest addition, Bumpy the orphaned hippo. This was his flight down to Kaluku. He was a perfect passenger – he scrambled right into Keeper Joseph's lap and spent most of the trip chattering in little hippo grunts!Bumpy is very new to the fold… pic.twitter.com/kGBzxW7a2Z

While the Trust hopes he’ll successfully integrate with other hippos in the area once he’s older, for now, little Bumpy is enjoying the sweet life with his caretakers, splashing in kiddie pools and napping in bean bags.

payload.title: Orvoksi jäänyt virtahevonpoikanen hoidetaan käsin Keniassa
payload.summary: Keniassa pelastettu vastasyntynyt virtahevonpoikanen on viety villieläinten hoitopaikkaan, jossa sen hoidosta vastaavat eläintenhoitajat. Bumpyksi nimetty poikanen löydettiin kuolleen emonsa läheltä Naivashan alueella.
payload.content:
Keniassa orvoksi jäänyt virtahevonpoikanen on pelastettu ja viety käsin hoidettavaksi villieläinten hoitopaikkaan. Bumpyksi nimetty poikanen löydettiin 2. toukokuuta 2026 Naivashan Oloiden Resortin alueelta eteläisessä Keski-Keniassa. Lähdetietojen mukaan se oli aivan kuolleen emonsa luona, kun viranomaiset ja eläintenhoitoon erikoistuneet toimijat saivat ilmoituksen tapauksesta.

## Poikanen löydettiin emonsa läheltä

Tapaus tuli viranomaisten tietoon, kun alueelta ilmoitettiin orvoksi jääneestä virtahevonpoikasesta. Kenya Wildlife Servicen eläinlääkintä- ja kiinniottotiimi hälytettiin paikalle. Etsintöjen yhteydessä löydettiin sekä poikanen että sen kuollut emo.

Kuvauksen mukaan poikanen oli pysytellyt aivan emonsa lähellä ja tökkinyt tätä epätoivoisesti. Poikanen on saanut nimekseen Bumpy. Sheldrick Wildlife Trustin mukaan se oli jäädessään orvoksi vain muutaman päivän ikäinen.

Näin nuoren poikasen tilanne on erityisen haavoittuva, koska se ei pysty selviytymään luonnossa yksin ilman emon antamaa suojaa ja hoivaa. Tämän vuoksi Bumpy siirrettiin villieläinten hoitopaikkaan, jossa eläintenhoitajat vastaavat sen päivittäisestä hoidosta.

## Käsin kasvattaminen vaatii jatkuvaa seurantaa

Bumpyn hoito on nyt Sheldrick Wildlife Trustin hoitajien vastuulla. Käsin kasvattaminen tarkoittaa käytännössä sitä, että hoitajien on huolehdittava poikasen ruokinnasta, seurannasta ja perustarpeista tilanteessa, jossa emo ei enää voi huolehtia siitä.

Paketin tiedoissa ei kerrota emon kuolinsyytä eikä poikasen tarkkaa terveydentilaa pelastuksen jälkeen. Tiedossa on kuitenkin, että poikanen oli löydettäessä hyvin nuori ja että sen pelastaminen tapahtui sen jälkeen, kun ilmoitukset orvosta virtahevonpoikasesta tavoittivat Kenya Wildlife Servicen tiimin.

## Nopea ilmoitus auttoi pelastuksessa

Tapaus korostaa sitä, miten tärkeää luonnonvaraisten eläinten poikkeavista tilanteista ilmoittaminen voi olla. Kun muutaman päivän ikäinen virtahevonpoikanen jää ilman emoaan, avun saaminen nopeasti voi ratkaista sen, saadaanko poikanen turvaan vai jääkö se yksin luontoon.

Bumpyn jatko riippuu nyt hoitajien työstä ja siitä, miten poikanen sopeutuu käsin kasvatettavaksi. Käytettävissä olevien tietojen perusteella sen hoito jatkuu Keniassa villieläinten hoitopaikassa.

Poikanen löydettiin 2. toukokuuta 2026 Naivashan Oloiden Resortin alueelta.
Sheldrick Wildlife Trustin hoitajat kasvattavat poikasta nyt käsin.
